name: Pixel Art
visualIdentity: Explicitly named pixel art with a 16-bit sprite appearance: low logical resolution, limited palette, whole-pixel placement and deliberate clusters. Optional examples are 320×180 and 32 colors; neither is mandatory.
suitableUses: Use for sprites and fixed-grid scenes. Explicitly suggested hybrids: style-105 beat-table timing for chiptune videos, game trailers and loops; style-077 isometric tiles for city-builder explainers and maps. Interactive HTML can use a fixed-resolution canvas with integer scaling. These are suggestions, not guarantees of fit.
limitations: Avoid smoothing, non-integer scaling, antialiased edges, arbitrary sprite rotation and post-effects that blend palette indices. Keep cycling discrete and silhouettes fixed; do not move every sprite on every beat or use full-screen flashing swaps. Six suggested colors are not canonical: supplied or approved palettes and style color limits take precedence. Contrast checks cover pairs only; inspect actual composites.
palette: Optional six-color suggestion: background #18253A, foreground #F3EBD3, accents #426A76, #8AA386, #D3A45E, #B56D6F. Preserve exact task, brand, reference and asset colors and semantic roles; normalize equivalents only. Keep discrete colors, no gradient or interpolation; derive shades only within the approved budget. Suggested text pairs: foreground on background (12.923:1), foreground on accent_1 (4.961:1), background on accent_2 (5.616:1), background on accent_3 (6.773:1); background on accent_4 is 3.944:1 and decorative only. Recheck real composites.
motionAndInteraction: Animate key poses with few in-betweens; hold poses and preserve authored exposure cadence. Cycle selected palette indices for water, neon or day/night without changing silhouettes. Scale by integer factors with smoothing off; distinguish pose rate from delivery frame rate. Video state must derive from seekable composition time, not live input. Interactive HTML may use pointer, scroll, keyboard or touch when appropriate, with bounded behavior and reduced-motion support. Optional beat hybrid uses saved beat tables, not drifting live analysis. Isometric hybrid moves tile by tile on 2:1 lines. Chapter/story patterns can coordinate progress, copy and states, but only when meaningful and reversible.
audio: No fixed soundtrack is specified. Suggest music, voice, effects, ambience or silence for the topic and audience; honor supplied assets and requirements. Beat-synced music is an optional hybrid. Keep speech clear, avoid clipping and competing vocals, and verify sync.
assetRequirements: Create indexed sprites or pixel clusters on a fixed-resolution offscreen canvas; separate palette indices from colors. Aseprite can author sprites, palettes and frame animation and export sheets or numbered PNGs. Canvas 2D is the direct renderer; PixiJS optionally composites sprites and particles, and p5.js can draw deterministic low-resolution layers. Prepare assets, fonts and cached state before assembly. Confirm eye layers or a rig before gaze tracking; otherwise omit it or use static expressions.
combinations: Pixel Art alone suits fixed-grid scenes. style-105 adds beat-table scheduling; style-077 adds a strict 2:1 isometric tile grid, crisp separate labels and the primary six-color palette, while avoiding 3D perspective. Optional narrative patterns: motion-012 for a meaningful reversible chapter handoff; motion-015 for ordered story states with reading holds. Use motion-006 only with suitable readable eyes and layers; it is bounded character gaze, not viewer tracking. Reject unsupported geometry or conflicting progress drivers.
productionApproach: Choose renderer and motion method for pixel fidelity and action first; each animated property has one owner. Canvas 2D is direct, Aseprite supports authoring, PixiJS is optional compositing, and p5.js is optional procedural drawing with explicit-time redraw, seeded state and seek checks. Use HyperFrames as primary for assembly, seekable timing, media/audio sync, validation and export; Remotion only if unavailable or a verified limitation blocks a required capability, recording the reason. Neither replaces the style renderer. Drive layers from shared time, disable smoothing, verify palette, contrast, aliasing, backward/direct seeks and decoded output. These routes are suggestions, not claims about source-video tooling.
